name: Shrink a target
summary: On a key, the user shrinks one enemy vehicle or ship for a while. The shrunk target becomes quicker, moving and firing faster, but it is a toy for the duration: it deals only a fraction of its normal damage, reaches and sees much less, takes double damage from everything, loses any crushing of its own and can be run over by any vehicle that crushes. Many shots also tend to miss its smaller body. Infantry are immune. The shrink does no damage by itself and wears off if nobody follows up, so it is a setup for teammates, above all for heavy vehicles that crush, and a way to blunt the biggest threat on the field.
counterplay: Pull the shrunk vehicle back: it is faster while small, so it can drive out of the fight until the effect wears off.
Keep enemy crushers away from a shrunk teammate and cover it while it is fragile.

Kill the caster, above all from the air: in the source unit nothing it carries does damage and its freeze beam can't reach aircraft, so enemy fliers can bring it down freely; ground attackers risk being frozen first.
Bring infantry: soldiers are immune to the shrink.
Don't feed the setup: a shrunk vehicle that stays to trade shots deals little and takes double.

other_examples.note: An item that racers near the back of the pack can get: it shrinks every other racer for a while, making them slower and weaker, spinning them out and making them drop their items; full-size racers who drive into a shrunk one flatten it. In later games the shrink lasts longer on racers who are further ahead.

other_examples.game: extra:Super Smash Bros. Brawl / for Wii U and 3DS / Ultimate
other_examples.note: Touching it usually shrinks every other fighter for a set time: small fighters hit for less damage, weigh less and are launched further. It can backfire, shrinking the user or making the others giant, and a size-changing mushroom cancels it.

shooter_analogues.note: A fast-moving shot that does no damage but shrinks its target for a while; walking into a shrunk enemy stomps it flat. In multiplayer a shrunk player can't use any weapon and dies at once if another player steps on them, but a steroids pickup restores their size and blocks further shrinking. Mechanical enemies and bosses are immune.

player_translation.summary: Press Q on an enemy vehicle to shrink it for a few seconds: it gets faster, but hits like a toy, sees and reaches less, takes double damage and any crushing vehicle can run it over. Soldiers are immune.
as_user: You pick the biggest threat on the field and turn it into a nuisance: the super-heavy tank about to break your line suddenly fires pebbles.
You call the follow-up: tell your tanks to run it over, or your team to focus it while it takes double damage.
In the source unit the shrink reaches about twice as far as its other beam, so you hang back, time the shot and keep away from fire that can reach you.
Against a team on foot it does nothing, so you need to read the enemy roster.
as_target: Your vehicle visibly shrinks, your gun's reach and sight drop on the HUD, and a timer shows how long it lasts.
You get faster, so your best move is usually to retreat until you grow back, not to trade shots.
Watch for enemy crushers: their tracks are now deadly to you, and your own crushing is gone.
If a teammate is shrunk, cover them: they are fragile and easy prey for anything heavy.
teammates: A setup for crushers and focus fire: a shrunk vehicle takes double damage and any crushing vehicle can kill it by driving over it.
The shrunk player's team protects them and escorts them out until the effect wears off.
It gives a support unit a real answer to the enemy's heaviest vehicle, so both teams plan around who carries it.
controls: Q with an enemy vehicle under the cursor: a short lock-on line, then the beam fires; infantry targets show 'immune' and the key does nothing.
Wave variant: Q fires a pulse that shrinks every enemy vehicle in an area or cone, for a shorter time.
feedback: A shrunk vehicle is drawn at about half size with a bright pulsing outline, so it reads at once from above even in a crowd.
A countdown ring around the shrunk target, visible to both teams, and a growing-back flash when it ends.
Crushers see a 'crushable' icon over shrunk enemies in range; the shrunk player hears a warning when an enemy crusher comes close.
A high-pitched sound filter for the shrunk player's engine and weapon, the way Mario Kart raises shrunk racers' voices.
changes_from_rts: A player must see each change on the HUD (reach, damage, sight, damage taken), not only the smaller model, or the effect feels random.

Being crushed instantly by any crushing vehicle is a harsh death for a player; keep crushing for heavy vehicles and make it a very fast kill rather than a silent one, with a warning when a crusher closes in.
The shrunk target's extra speed is what gives it a way out; keep it, so the victim always has a choice: retreat now, or risk staying.
Infantry immunity stays: it keeps the shrink an anti-vehicle tool and gives teams on foot a clean counter.
Shots missing the smaller body (RA3's deviation on shells and rockets) should come from the real, smaller hitbox, not from a hidden accuracy penalty.

team_play.notes: The shrink does nothing alone: a teammate must crush or focus the target while it is small. It is a clean counter-pick against vehicle-heavy teams, and the victim's team must escort the shrunk vehicle to safety.

notes: Needs a timed status that scales the target's model, hitbox, weapon reach, sight and damage, and changes its armour multiplier, all reversible.
Crush rules must read the current size: a shrunk vehicle can be crushed by any crusher and crushes nothing itself.
Growing back in a tight space must push the unit to a free spot instead of trapping it in walls.
Multi-seat vehicles: every seat's weapon and HUD must reflect the shrink.
UI: a target timer, crushable icons for enemies, and a clear immune message for infantry targets.
Combined with crushers it is close to a delayed kill on any vehicle; the duration and the crush rule are the main levers.
Against T3 super-heavies it may be too efficient for a T2 support unit; scale duration by target tier.
Against infantry-heavy teams the unit carrying it is dead weight, which can make it feel bad to pick.
Speeding up the target can backfire if the shrunk vehicle uses the speed to reach and capture objectives.
From above, a shrunk vehicle could be mistaken for a smaller, lighter vehicle type; it needs an outline or colour that says 'shrunk'.
Players must know both sides of the change at once: faster, but weak and fragile.
In a crowded fight it may be unclear who can crush the shrunk target.

variants.name: Shrink beam
variants.summary: A targeted shot on one vehicle or ship: faster but feeble, fragile and crushable for a while; infantry immune.

variants.name: Shrink pulse
variants.summary: One pulse shrinks every enemy vehicle in an area or cone, for a shorter time than the single-target beam.
variants.seen_in: Mario Kart's Lightning and Smash Bros.'s Lightning Bolt shrink every opponent at once; a Red Alert 3 challenge map shrinks every unit on the field

adds_strengths.why: One pulse makes every enemy vehicle in the area feeble and fragile for a short while: they hit far softer, see and reach less, take double damage and can be run over.

variants.name: Threat-scaled shrink
variants.summary: The shrink lasts longer on enemies who are doing better, such as higher-tier vehicles or players on a kill streak.
variants.seen_in: Mario Kart's Lightning, which lasts longer on racers further ahead

variants.name: Shrink and stomp
variants.summary: Infantry can be shrunk too: a shrunk soldier can't fire for a short time and anything that walks or drives over it kills it; a cleanse or pickup restores its size.

adds_weaknesses.why: Does no damage itself; a shrunk soldier only dies if someone reaches and steps on it before the effect ends.

counters.why: Cuts the heaviest tanks down to a fraction of their firepower and makes them easy prey for crushers.
A shrunk crusher loses its crushing, and other crushers can run it over instead.
Shrinks soldiers too, who can't fire while small and die if anything steps on them.

countered_by.why: Fast targets shrunk get faster still and run out of reach before anyone can stomp them.

variants.name: Unstable shrink
variants.summary: Sometimes the effect backfires: it shrinks the user instead, or makes the target grow large and strong for a while.
variants.seen_in: Smash Bros.'s Lightning Bolt, which can shrink the user or enlarge the others

adds_strengths.why: Makes one enemy vehicle feeble and fragile for a while: it hits far softer, sees and reaches less, takes double damage and can be run over.

adds_weaknesses.why: Does no damage itself and nothing to infantry, and the shrunk vehicle moves faster, so without a follow-up it simply gets away.

counters.why: Cuts the heaviest tanks down to a fraction of their firepower and makes them easy prey for crushers.
A shrunk crusher loses its crushing, and other crushers can run it over instead.

countered_by.why: Soldiers are immune to the shrink, so a team on foot gives it nothing to work on.
A fast vehicle gets faster still when shrunk and drives out of the fight until the effect wears off.

open_questions: Should shrunk vehicles be crushable by any crushing vehicle, as in RA3, or only by heavier ones? (Recommended: any crusher, with a warning to the shrunk player.)
Should infantry stay immune (RA3), or should a high-spice variant shrink soldiers too (Duke Nukem 3D)?
Should passengers inside a shrunk vehicle be affected, for example thrown out, or ride along unchanged?
Can a repair tool or a cleanse end the shrink early, giving the victim's team a rescue?

shooter_fit.reason: A size change reads instantly from above, it creates a clear setup for crushers and focus fire, and the victim keeps a choice (flee faster or stay weak); it only works against vehicles and needs careful crush rules.
